text: What to do if you feel hated in your own family just for being a man? Today, a tough question. Hey, I thought I could use some of your wisdom. I grew up as the only brother in a family with four sisters. Two of them I constantly get into arguments with because they go and rant about the typical men stuff and how they're all evil and whenever I try to defend myself, I just get ganged up on by the other women in my family. I feel like I'm drifting apart from my family every conversation and I feel less appreciated in my family because I'm a male. They are my family so I can't just let them go but I'm not sure what I can do. This is a difficult situation because family is not something you choose. You can choose your friends and the women you date but family is just given to you. Still, there are a few things you not only can do but in my opinion should do and the first one is this. Become independent. You didn't mention your age so let's assume you are around 18. Here's the thing. Until you become independent, until you stop depending on your family for housing, food and money, there's not much you can really do. You kind of have to follow their rules and go along with their narrative. That is just how life works when someone else is paying for your life. So whatever your age is, take this as your sign to become independent. Find a job, start supporting yourself and move out. Honestly, I recommend this to every man. Separate yourself from your family as early as possible because it teaches you responsibility. But in your case, it is even more important. Once you have that distance and no longer depend on them, then you can actually decide how you want to handle things. For example, if it is only two of your sisters causing the issue, you can limit your interaction with them and focus on spending time with your parents or your other sisters if they treat you well. Or you can stay civil overall and only see your family on holidays. With distance, you can navigate the situation on your own terms. But here is something important. You still need to put yourself first and have boundaries. Even, or I would say especially, with your own family. The problem is that having boundaries is hard when you depend on the people you are sitting with. Once you are independent, it becomes much easier. Then you can openly say, look, sisters, or look, parents, I do not want to hear you talk about me or other men like this in my presence. This bothers me, this hurts me, this makes me uncomfortable. If they listen to you, great. But if they do not, then be ready to stand by your boundaries. Because if you say it, they disregard it, and you just go along with it, then what are your boundaries even worth? So in short, become independent first, then see how things go. Once you are on your own, you can decide what level of interaction still feels comfortable for you. Before that, well, you are dependent, so you kind of have to put up with things. That is just life.
